properties.name: A fix says whether it corrected the cause or worked around it, so "how much of this is standing on a patch?" is a question the design can answer
properties.statement:
A change that repairs something must record WHICH KIND OF REPAIR IT WAS — the cause corrected, or the symptom worked around — and a workaround must name the correction it is standing in for. The design must then be able to answer, without asking a person: what is still resting on a patch?

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`, which the guard matched, and the split is the point rather than a technicality. The RULE is how the people building reflow2 work; it binds this project and can never bind anyone else's. This REQUIREMENT is the product carrying the same philosophy, so every project using reflow2 inherits the question. Anthony asked for exactly that on 2026-08-17: "this is my philosophy on how to build something - so ensuring that it is built into the design of reflow2." A rule states it; a requirement makes it something reflow2 DOES.

⭐ THE QUESTION HE ASKED WAS UNANSWERABLE WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN, and that is the whole case. "I'm not sure how many fixes have been patches versus going back to the drawing board, planning how it should have been done correctly, and then re-implementing proper fix." MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17: 472 ChangeEvents across eleven change types — new_feature 156, test_failure_fix 101, refactor 89, scope_change 59, baseline_established 25, resync 14, defect_fix 11, requirement_creep 6, deprecation 6, constraint_change 4, performance_optimization 1. EVERY ONE OF THOSE NAMES WHAT MOVED. NOT ONE SAYS WHETHER IT WAS THE RIGHT FIX. A `test_failure_fix` is equally the record of a root-cause rewrite and of a shim that made a red test green, and nothing downstream can tell them apart.

CHECKED AND FOUND NOT TO BE THE PROBLEM, so the fix is not aimed at the wrong thing: `test_failure_fix` is the DEFAULT for a `design_holds` drift accept, so the obvious hypothesis was that the commonest fix type is an unchosen default. It is not — 55 of the 101 are auto-minted accepts and ALL 55 carry written reasons, with 46 more named deliberately. The discipline is there. THE VOCABULARY IS WHAT IS MISSING.

⭐ THE SHAPE IS ALREADY PROVEN ONE LAYER OVER, which is why this is buildable rather than aspirational. `dec:two-sided-accept` made accepting drift a two-sided act: you say the content moved AND you take a position (`design_holds` / `design_updated`), because "accept the file, leave the design alone, say nothing" is the option that erodes a design into fiction. A FIX IS THE SAME SHAPE AND IS CURRENTLY ONE-SIDED. Silent patching should be as impossible as silent drift-accept, for the identical reason.

WHAT IS OWED, in the order it is worth building:
(a) A repair records its ROOT DISPOSITION — cause corrected, or symptom contained. Not defaulted, on `req:defaults-do-not-assert`: whether a fix reached the cause is a judgement, and inventing an answer records a claim nobody made.
(b) A contained symptom NAMES WHAT THE PROPER FIX WOULD BE. This is what turns a patch from an invisible cost into a stated debt with somewhere to be read. A workaround nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from a design decision six weeks later.
(c) The count is REPORTABLE — what still rests on a patch, and where. That is the question above, answered by the graph rather than by anyone's memory.

⚠️ WHAT THIS MUST NOT BECOME, stated now because the failure mode is predictable and this project has met it twice this month. It must NOT judge. reflow2 records the claim and counts it; the human decides whether a patch was right (`dec:report-dont-judge`, `dec:three-party-checks`). A detector that tried to INFER "this was a patch" from graph shape would be exactly the confident answer to a nearby question that `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` was written about. And a workaround is often the CORRECT call under a deadline — the requirement is that it be VISIBLE, never that it be forbidden.

⚠️ HONEST LIMIT, and it bounds what can ever be claimed here: this records what the author SAYS about their fix. It cannot detect a patch someone reports as a correction. That makes it the same class of instrument as `provenance` and the drift dispositions — worth having because the alternative is no signal at all, and worth never overselling.

═══ SETTLED — DO NOT RE-ASK (corrected 2026-09-09) ═══

🛑 THE RETRO QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND HAS BEEN SINCE THE DAY THIS REQUIREMENT WAS WRITTEN. `dec:the-patch-record-binds-forward-not-backward`, ACCEPTED 2026-08-17 on Anthony's word: FORWARD ONLY. The events already on the record are NOT classified as patches or corrections and no backfill pass will be run over them, because nobody remembers which of them reached its cause and an agent reconstructing that from diffs would produce edges that are queryable and unfounded.

⚠️ THIS PARAGRAPH REPLACES A "NOT YET DECIDED" ONE THAT OUTLIVED ITS OWN DECISION BY THREE WEEKS, and the cost was real: on 2026-09-09 a session read the stale text, believed the fork was open, and put it to Anthony a second time. He gave the same answer. The lesson is not about this requirement — it is that PROSE STATING AN OPEN QUESTION MUST BE RETIRED WHEN THE QUESTION IS SETTLED, and that nothing in reflow2 checks a Requirement's statement against the Decisions governing it the way `prose_currency` checks a Verification's description against its status.

WHERE THE BOUNDARIES NOW SIT, because the two limbs shipped three weeks apart and one cutoff does not serve both:
  • the REPAIR DISPOSITION (clause a/b) — on the ChangeEvent, via record_change's `repair` and `stands_in_for`, read by `repair_report`. Shipped 2026-09-09. Binds from its own landing under the parent ruling.
  • the CAUSE EDGE (a fix joined to what it closed) — enforced by the `fix_without_recorded_cause` detector, shipped 2026-09-06. Binds from 2026-09-06 under `dec:the-cause-discipline-binds-forward-not-backward`, which parks the 228 pre-detector fixes rather than acknowledging the finding, so the detector stays live for everything after it.

STILL GENUINELY OPEN, and narrowed from the original wording rather than dropped: whether the root disposition should ALSO ride the artifact accept, not only the ChangeEvent. It landed on the ChangeEvent; nothing has decided the accept half either way.
